# `oximux` CLI reference

Every command and option below is read from the parser itself, so this
file cannot drift from what the binary accepts. Regenerate with
`scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh > docs/cli-reference.md`; CI fails if the result
differs from what is committed.

## Exit codes

| Code | Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `ok` | The command succeeded. |
| 1 | `error` | The command ran and failed. |
| 2 | `usage` | The arguments were wrong; nothing was attempted. |
| 3 | `host_unreachable` | No host answered. Retrying may help. |
| 4 | `timeout` | The host did not reply in time. |
| 5 | `access_denied` | The caller is not allowed to do this. Retrying will not help. |
| 6 | `data_dir_held` | `serve` only: another host already holds the data directory. Do not restart on it. |
| 7 | `pending_user` | Waiting on a person (a `sim` verb before the user allowed agents on the device). Wait, then retry. |
| 8 | `target_not_found` | No session or terminal has that id, or the prefix matches more than one (the candidates go to stderr). Nothing was sent. |
| 130 | `interrupted` | Stopped with Ctrl+C (a streaming verb such as `events`). |

## Conventions

- **JSON output** — --json prints {"ok":true,"data":…} or {"ok":false,"error":{code,message,next_steps}} on stdout; `error.data` is present only when a failure leaves something addressable behind (e.g. session_id on a turn timeout)
- **Async contract** — send-style verbs return when the host ACCEPTS the work, not when the agent finishes
- **Session scope** — when OXIMUX_SESSION_ID is set, this CLI reaches only that session

## Global options

These apply to every command.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | no | Emit machine-readable JSON on stdout (one convention, every verb). Streaming verbs (run/send/attach/wait) emit NDJSON event lines, then a final result object |
| `--dir` | yes | The host's runtime directory (where its control socket lives). Defaults to this machine's OxiMux data directory. Local hosts only |
| `--host` | yes | Talk to a paired remote host instead of this machine (see `oximux hosts ls`). Also read from $OXIMUX_HOST; a recorded default applies when neither is set. With no hosts paired, everything talks to this machine — no configuration needed |
| `--timeout` | yes | Seconds to wait for a host reply before giving up (exit 4). For `wait`, this is the overall bound on the wait itself. It does NOT bound an agent's turn: `run`/`send` stream until the turn ends, and `attach` until Ctrl+C. Bound a turn with `run`/`send --turn-timeout` |

## Commands

### `oximux status`

Is a host reachable, and what is it running? (versions, session counts)

_No arguments._

### `oximux ls`

List the host's agent sessions

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all-hosts` | no | List every paired host's sessions, and this machine's, in one table with a host column. An unreachable host becomes a warning row and the rest still print (exit 0); --strict makes that exit 3 instead |
| `--strict` | no | Fail (exit 3) if any host could not be reached |

### `oximux run`

Start an agent session and send it a prompt.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<PROMPT>` | yes | The prompt to send, or `-` to read it from stdin |
| `--agent` | yes | Which configured agent to start (default: the host's default agent) |
| `--model` | yes | Switch the session to this model before sending the prompt |
| `--mode` | yes | Switch the session to this permission mode before sending the prompt (ids from `model ls`). Without it the session starts in the backend's default, which for most agents asks before each tool — and an unattended `run` then streams up to the request and waits there, since only a decision can end that turn. `acceptEdits` is the usual choice for a scripted run |
| `--cwd` | yes | Working directory for the session (default: the current directory) |
| `--worktree` | yes | Create a worktree with this slug under the project first, and start the session inside it. The project is the `--cwd` (or current) directory, which must be a project the host knows |
| `--output-schema` | yes | Hold the final answer to a JSON Schema — a file path, or the schema itself as inline JSON. The agent is re-prompted with the validation errors up to twice; a still-invalid answer exits 1. Prints the validated JSON. Needs the turn, so it cannot be combined with --bg |
| `--turn-timeout` | yes | Give up on the turn after this many seconds (exit 4). The agent is left running — only this command stops waiting. Without it the stream is unbounded, which is right for a terminal and wrong for a CI job, since a turn parked on a permission request ends only when something decides it. The global --timeout does NOT bound the turn; it bounds one host reply |
| `--stalled-after` | yes | Give up if the agent produces nothing for this many seconds (exit 4). This bounds PROGRESS, not total time: a turn working steadily runs as long as it needs, while a wedged one is caught in seconds. `--turn-timeout` cannot tell those apart — raise it and a wedged agent burns the lot, lower it and a thinking one is cut off. Use both: a generous turn budget with a tight stall budget |
| `--bg` | no | Print the session id and exit instead of staying attached |

### `oximux attach`

Stream a session's live events to the terminal.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SESSION>` | yes | The session id, or a unique prefix of it (see `oximux ls`) |
| `--from` | yes | Replay retained events after this sequence number first (default: attach at the live edge) |

### `oximux send`

Send a prompt into an existing session.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SESSION>` | yes | The session id, or a unique prefix of it (see `oximux ls`) |
| `<PROMPT>` | yes | The prompt to send, or `-` to read it from stdin |
| `--output-schema` | yes | Hold the final answer to a JSON Schema — a file path, or the schema itself as inline JSON. The agent is re-prompted with the validation errors up to twice; a still-invalid answer exits 1. Prints the validated JSON. Needs the turn, so it cannot be combined with --no-wait |
| `--turn-timeout` | yes | Give up on the turn after this many seconds (exit 4). The agent is left running — only this command stops waiting. Without it the stream is unbounded, which is right for a terminal and wrong for a CI job, since a turn parked on a permission request ends only when something decides it. The global --timeout does NOT bound the turn; it bounds one host reply |
| `--stalled-after` | yes | Give up if the agent produces nothing for this many seconds (exit 4). This bounds PROGRESS, not total time: a turn working steadily runs as long as it needs, while a wedged one is caught in seconds. `--turn-timeout` cannot tell those apart — raise it and a wedged agent burns the lot, lower it and a thinking one is cut off. Use both: a generous turn budget with a tight stall budget |
| `--no-wait` | no | Return as soon as the host accepts the prompt |

### `oximux wait`

Block until a session reaches a state (or --timeout expires, exit 4).

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SESSION>` | yes | The session id, or a unique prefix of it (see `oximux ls`) |
| `--until` | yes | The state to wait for |
| `--stalled-after` | yes | Give up if the session produces nothing for this many seconds (exit 4, distinct message). Bounds progress, not total time |

### `oximux transcript`

Fetch a session's full transcript (paged under the hood)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SESSION>` | yes | The session id, or a unique prefix of it (see `oximux ls`) |

### `oximux stop`

Interrupt a session's in-flight turn. The session stays open

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SESSION>` | yes | The session id, or a unique prefix of it (see `oximux ls`) |

### `oximux steer`

Redirect a mid-turn agent with additional guidance. Needs a backend with a mid-turn message queue; claude and codex have none and refuse it, so on those use `stop` and then `send`

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SESSION>` | yes | The session id, or a unique prefix of it (see `oximux ls`) |
| `<TEXT>` | yes | The guidance to inject |

### `oximux permit`

_No arguments._

#### `oximux permit ls`

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SESSION>` | yes | The session id, or a unique prefix of it (see `oximux ls`) |

#### `oximux permit allow`

Approve a pending permission request.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SESSION>` | yes | The session id, or a unique prefix of it (see `oximux ls`) |
| `<REQUEST>` | yes | The request id (from `permit ls`; default: the latest pending) |
| `--input` | yes | Replace the tool's input with this JSON object before approving. `permit ls --json` prints the proposed input to edit from. The object is passed through as given, so it must carry every field the tool needs — it replaces the input, it does not merge into it |

#### `oximux permit deny`

Deny a pending permission request

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SESSION>` | yes | The session id, or a unique prefix of it (see `oximux ls`) |
| `<REQUEST>` | yes | The request id (from `permit ls`; default: the latest pending) |
| `--message` | yes | The reason shown to the agent |

#### `oximux permit answer`

Answer a pending multiple-choice question.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SESSION>` | yes | The session id, or a unique prefix of it (see `oximux ls`) |
| `<REQUEST>` | yes | The request id (from `permit ls`; default: the latest pending) |
| `--answer` | yes | One answer per question, in order (label, 1-based number, or text) |

### `oximux term`

See and attach to the host's terminals

_No arguments._

#### `oximux term ls`

List the host's terminals

_No arguments._

#### `oximux term attach`

Attach to a terminal: keystrokes go to the host, output comes back. Ctrl+] detaches; the terminal keeps running.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<PTY>` | yes | The terminal id, or a unique prefix of it (see `term ls`) |

#### `oximux term send`

Type into a terminal without attaching: text first, then `--keys`, then Enter if `--enter`. Nothing is added — no newline unless asked.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<PTY>` | yes | The terminal id, or a unique prefix of it (see `term ls`) |
| `<TEXT>` | yes | Text to type, exactly as given |
| `--keys` | yes | Named keys to press after the text, in order. Repeatable, or comma-separated: `--keys up,up,enter`. Names: enter, tab, esc, backspace, space, up, down, left, right, home, end, pgup, pgdn, insert, delete, f1-f12, ctrl-<a-z>, alt-<char> (any but a comma) |
| `--stdin` | no | Read the text to type from stdin instead of the argument |
| `--enter` | no | Press Enter after everything else |
| `--app-cursor` | no | Send cursor keys in application mode (`ESC O A` rather than `ESC [ A`) |

### `oximux events`

Stream session changes as they happen: one line per session added, removed, or changed (title, model, waiting for permission). Runs until Ctrl+C (exit 130), or until `--until` is met (exit 0).

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--session` | yes | Only this session (its id, or a unique prefix of it) |
| `--until` | yes | Exit 0 as soon as a watched session reaches this state |

### `oximux agent`

Install, remove, and inspect the status hooks that let agent CLIs report what they are doing.

_No arguments._

#### `oximux agent hooks`

Turn the status hooks on, off, or report what is installed

_No arguments._

##### `oximux agent hooks status`

Report, per agent, whether OxiMux's hooks are installed and which file was read to decide.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--agent` | yes | One agent slug (see `agent hooks status`). Default: all of them |

##### `oximux agent hooks on`

Install the hooks, merging them into whatever is already in each file.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--agent` | yes | One agent slug. Default: all of them |

##### `oximux agent hooks off`

Remove the hooks, leaving anything OxiMux did not write exactly where it is — including in a file OxiMux would otherwise delete outright, which is read first and kept if it holds someone else's hooks.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--agent` | yes | One agent slug. Default: all of them |

### `oximux worktree`

Create, list, and remove project worktrees on the host

_No arguments._

#### `oximux worktree create`

Create a worktree (and its branch) under a project. The host derives the on-disk location; the reply carries it

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SLUG>` | yes | The worktree slug (becomes the branch, under the configured prefix) |
| `--project` | yes | The project's root path (default: the current directory). Must be a project the host knows (see `projects ls`) |
| `--from` | yes | Cut the new branch from this ref instead of the repository's default branch — a branch, a tag, or a SHA |
| `--branch` | yes | Check out an existing LOCAL branch into the new worktree. No branch is created and no prefix is applied |

#### `oximux worktree ls`

List worktrees (all projects unless --project narrows it)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project` | yes | A project root path to narrow to (see `projects ls`) |

#### `oximux worktree rm`

Remove a worktree by id (see `worktree ls`). Refused (not forced) when the worktree has uncommitted changes.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | yes | The worktree id (from `worktree ls`) |

#### `oximux worktree set`

Say what is happening in a worktree — a one-line comment, a work phase, or both. Meant to be called by the agent working there, as it works.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | yes | The worktree id (from `worktree ls`) |
| `--comment` | yes | The status line — what is happening here right now. `""` clears it |
| `--phase` | yes | The work phase: todo, in-progress, in-review, or done. `""` clears it. An unrecognised value is refused |

### `oximux schedule`

Scheduled agent runs: create, list, pause, and fire them on the host.

_No arguments._

#### `oximux schedule create`

Create a schedule. Exactly one cadence flag is required

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<PROMPT>` | yes | The prompt each fire sends into its fresh session |
| `--name` | yes | A name for the schedule (shown in lists) |
| `--cwd` | yes | Working directory for each run's session (default: the current directory) |
| `--agent` | yes | Which configured agent runs it (default: the host's default agent) |
| `--every` | yes | Fire every N minutes (minimum 5) |
| `--daily` | yes | Fire daily at this local time, e.g. 09:00 |
| `--weekly` | yes | Fire weekly at this day and local time, e.g. "mon 09:00" |
| `--cron` | yes | Fire on a 5-field cron expression, e.g. "0 9 * * 1-5" for weekdays at 09:00. Evaluated in the HOST's local time, like every other cadence. Needs a host on protocol v23 or newer. |

#### `oximux schedule ls`

List schedules with cadence, next fire, and state

_No arguments._

#### `oximux schedule logs`

A schedule's recent run history, newest first

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | yes | The schedule id (from `schedule ls`) |
| `--limit` | yes | How many runs to show |

#### `oximux schedule pause`

Pause a schedule (it keeps its history; resume re-arms from now)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | yes | The schedule id (from `schedule ls`) |

#### `oximux schedule resume`

Resume a paused schedule — armed forward from now, no catch-up fire

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | yes | The schedule id (from `schedule ls`) |

#### `oximux schedule run-once`

Fire a schedule immediately. Its cadence is untouched: the next scheduled occurrence still fires on time. Waits for the run to start (or fail to) and reports the recorded outcome

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | yes | The schedule id (from `schedule ls`) |

#### `oximux schedule rm`

Delete a schedule and its run history.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | yes | The schedule id (from `schedule ls`) |

### `oximux team`

#### `oximux team run`

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |

### `oximux state`

The shared coordination blackboard: versioned keys agents read and write.

_No arguments._

#### `oximux state get`

Read one key. An unset key prints `(unset)` and exits 0 — "nobody has claimed this" is an answer, not a failure.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<KEY>` | yes | The key |

#### `oximux state set`

Write one key. The value must be JSON

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<KEY>` | yes | The key |
| `<VALUE>` | yes | The value, as JSON (e.g. '"claimed"', '{"n":1}') |
| `--if-version` | yes | Write only if the stored version is exactly this — 0 means "only if absent". A mismatch exits 5 and prints the current value |

#### `oximux state delete`

Delete one key.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<KEY>` | yes | The key |

#### `oximux state watch`

Print every matching key, then stream changes until Ctrl+C.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--prefix` | yes | Only keys starting with this (default: every key) |
| `--since` | yes | Resume after this sequence number (from a previous watch's `seq`). Without it the watch starts from the board as it stands now |

#### `oximux sim tap`

Tap a point (x y, in points from the top-left), an @eN ref, or the element with an accessibility label or identifier

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<X>` | yes |  |
| `<Y>` | yes |  |
| `--label` | yes | An accessibility label: exact match first, then a case-insensitive substring |
| `--id` | yes | An accessibility identifier, exact |
| `--exact` | no | Match the label or identifier exactly (no substring fallback) |
| `--role` | yes | Only elements of this role (`Button`, `TextField`, … as `ax` prints them); exact |
| `--nth` | yes | The Nth such element on screen, from 0, in `ax` order |
| `--settle` | no | Wait for the screen to go idle, then print what changed: `+` appeared, `-` went, with `@eN` refs to act on next |
| `--settle-timeout` | yes | The longest to wait for it (default 5000 on a simulator, 6000 on Android or an iPhone, 8000 for launch and open-url; at most 60000) |

#### `oximux sim swipe`

Swipe from (x1, y1) to (x2, y2), in points. Starting at the very bottom edge is the home gesture

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<X1>` | yes |  |
| `<Y1>` | yes |  |
| `<X2>` | yes |  |
| `<Y2>` | yes |  |
| `--duration` | yes |  |
| `--settle` | no | Wait for the screen to go idle, then print what changed: `+` appeared, `-` went, with `@eN` refs to act on next |
| `--settle-timeout` | yes | The longest to wait for it (default 5000 on a simulator, 6000 on Android or an iPhone, 8000 for launch and open-url; at most 60000) |

#### `oximux sim type`

Type text into the focused field (or, after an @eN ref, into that element). Non-ASCII text is pasted

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<TEXT>` | yes |  |
| `--paste` | no | Paste through the device clipboard instead of typing key by key |
| `--settle` | no | Wait for the screen to go idle, then print what changed: `+` appeared, `-` went, with `@eN` refs to act on next |
| `--settle-timeout` | yes | The longest to wait for it (default 5000 on a simulator, 6000 on Android or an iPhone, 8000 for launch and open-url; at most 60000) |

#### `oximux sim button`

Press a hardware button

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<BUTTON>` | yes |  |
| `--settle` | no | Wait for the screen to go idle, then print what changed: `+` appeared, `-` went, with `@eN` refs to act on next |
| `--settle-timeout` | yes | The longest to wait for it (default 5000 on a simulator, 6000 on Android or an iPhone, 8000 for launch and open-url; at most 60000) |

#### `oximux sim rotate`

Rotate the device

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<TO>` | yes |  |
| `--settle` | no | Wait for the screen to go idle, then print what changed: `+` appeared, `-` went, with `@eN` refs to act on next |
| `--settle-timeout` | yes | The longest to wait for it (default 5000 on a simulator, 6000 on Android or an iPhone, 8000 for launch and open-url; at most 60000) |

#### `oximux sim launch`

Launch an installed app by bundle id (Android: package name)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<BUNDLE_ID>` | yes |  |
| `--relaunch` | no | Terminate it first, so it starts fresh |
| `--settle` | no | Wait for the screen to go idle, then print what changed: `+` appeared, `-` went, with `@eN` refs to act on next |
| `--settle-timeout` | yes | The longest to wait for it (default 5000 on a simulator, 6000 on Android or an iPhone, 8000 for launch and open-url; at most 60000) |

#### `oximux sim open-url`

Open a URL (http, https, or an app's own scheme; not file:)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<URL>` | yes |  |
| `--settle` | no | Wait for the screen to go idle, then print what changed: `+` appeared, `-` went, with `@eN` refs to act on next |
| `--settle-timeout` | yes | The longest to wait for it (default 5000 on a simulator, 6000 on Android or an iPhone, 8000 for launch and open-url; at most 60000) |

#### `oximux sim wait`

Wait for an element to appear (or, --gone, to go): exit 0 once it does, 4 when time runs out

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<R>` | yes | An `@eN` ref |
| `--label` | yes | An accessibility label: exact match first, then a case-insensitive substring (only exact with --exact) |
| `--id` | yes | An accessibility identifier, exact |
| `--exact` | no | Match the label or identifier exactly (no substring fallback) |
| `--role` | yes | Only elements of this role (`Button`, `TextField`, … as `ax` prints them); exact |
| `--nth` | yes | The Nth such element on screen, from 0, in `ax` order |
| `--gone` | no | Wait for it to go away instead |
| `--timeout-ms` | yes | Give up after this long (at most 60000) |

#### `oximux sim assert`

Check an element once: exit 0 if it holds, 1 (assert-failed) saying what was found if not

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<R>` | yes | An `@eN` ref |
| `--label` | yes | An accessibility label: exact match first, then a case-insensitive substring (only exact with --exact) |
| `--id` | yes | An accessibility identifier, exact |
| `--exact` | no | Match the label or identifier exactly (no substring fallback) |
| `--role` | yes | Only elements of this role (`Button`, `TextField`, … as `ax` prints them); exact |
| `--nth` | yes | The Nth such element on screen, from 0, in `ax` order |
| `--gone` | no | It is not on screen |
| `--text` | yes | Its text (a field's value, else its label) is exactly this |
| `--enabled` | no | It is on screen and enabled |

#### `oximux sim install`

Install a built .app (inside this worktree or Xcode's DerivedData) or, on Android, an .apk inside this worktree

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<PATH>` | yes |  |

#### `oximux sim shutdown`

Shut the simulator down. A simulator the user booted is refused without --force

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--force` | no |  |

#### `oximux sim location`

Set or clear where the device says it is

_No arguments._

##### `oximux sim location set`

Pretend to be at LAT LON (degrees; south and west are negative)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<LAT>` | yes |  |
| `<LON>` | yes |  |

##### `oximux sim location clear`

Stop pretending (a simulator only; an emulator keeps its last place)

_No arguments._

#### `oximux sim appearance`

Light or dark mode

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<MODE>` | yes |  |

#### `oximux sim privacy`

Grant, revoke or reset an app's permission (the app may restart)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ACTION>` | yes |  |
| `<SERVICE>` | yes | calendar, contacts, location, location-always, photos, photos-add, media-library, microphone, motion, reminders, siri, camera, notifications (what each platform has differs) |
| `--app` | yes | The app's bundle id (Android: package name). Required: nothing changes for every app at once |

#### `oximux sim push`

Deliver a push notification to an app (asked every time)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app` | yes | The app's bundle id |
| `<FILE>` | yes | The notification's JSON: an object with `aps` (at most 4096 bytes) |

#### `oximux sim status-bar`

A clean status bar for screenshots, or the real one back

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<MODE>` | yes |  |

#### `oximux sim erase`

Wipe the device to factory settings and boot it again (asked every time). A device the user booted is refused without --force

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--force` | no |  |

#### `oximux sim logs`

The device's recent log, one bounded read (default: the last 30s, 200 lines). A real Android phone needs --app

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--since` | yes | How far back: 30s, 5m, 1h (at most 1h) |
| `--app` | yes | One app's messages (bundle id; Android: package name). Required on a real Android phone; on a simulator, without it (or --grep) at most 10m (5m with info or debug) |
| `--grep` | yes | Only messages containing TEXT (ignoring case) |
| `--level` | yes | error: errors and faults only; info and debug add more |
| `--lines` | yes | The last N lines (at most 2000; the output is also cut to 64 KiB) |

#### `oximux sim crashes`

The device's recent crashes, each with its exception and top frames (default: the last 10m), and warnings short of a crash. A real Android phone needs --app

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--since` | yes | How far back: 30s, 10m, 1h (at most 1h) |
| `--app` | yes | One app's crashes (bundle id; Android: package name). Required on a real Android phone |

#### `oximux sim run`

Run a file of steps in order, stopping at the first that fails (its exit code is the run's). Steps that change device state ask the user once, before step 1

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<FILE>` | yes | The steps: one `oximux sim` command per line without the prefix (`tap --label "Sign in" --exact`), `#` comments. `-` reads stdin |
| `--settle` | no | Settle after every action step |
| `--from` | yes | Start at step N (from 1), e.g. to resume after exit 7 |

#### `oximux sim flow`

Record agent steps into a flow file that `sim run` replays, or export one

_No arguments._

##### `oximux sim flow start`

Record this worktree's agent verbs on its device, from now

_No arguments._

##### `oximux sim flow stop`

Stop recording: the steps are saved in OxiMux's data (private) and the path printed, or written to --out

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--out` | yes | Write the flow file here instead |

##### `oximux sim flow status`

Whether a recording runs, and its steps so far

_No arguments._

##### `oximux sim flow export`

Turn a flow file into another tool's format

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<FILE>` | yes | The flow file (`-` reads stdin) |
| `--maestro` | no | As Maestro YAML (the only format so far) |
| `--out` | yes | Write it here instead of stdout |
| `--app-id` | yes | The app the flow drives (default: the file's `# app`, else its first launch) |

#### `oximux sim exec`

Run a raw simctl (iOS simulator) or adb (Android) command on the attached device: `oximux sim exec -- ui appearance dark`. Off unless the user turns it on in Settings, asked every time, and limited to commands that touch only that device

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ARGV>` | yes | The command after `simctl` (iOS simulator) or `adb` (Android), after `--`, without the device: OxiMux adds the attached one |

#### `oximux sim net`

Shape an Android device's network: an emulator's speed, or offline and online (a real phone is asked every time). An iOS simulator shares the Mac's network and is never shaped

_No arguments._

##### `oximux sim net speed`

An Android emulator's network speed: gsm, hscsd, gprs, edge, umts, hsdpa, lte, evdo, full, or kbit/s. The emulator shapes only mobile data, so a speed below full turns its Wi-Fi off (full turns it on)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SPEED>` | yes |  |

##### `oximux sim net offline`

Turn off the device's Wi-Fi and mobile data (Android). `net online` turns them back on

_No arguments._

##### `oximux sim net online`

Turn the device's Wi-Fi and mobile data back on (Android)

_No arguments._

#### `oximux sim rn`

Look into the React Native app on the device through Metro: its requests, or a CPU profile

_No arguments._

##### `oximux sim rn network`

The React Native app's HTTP requests while it runs for a few seconds: method, status, time, size and URL (React Native 0.83 or later, in a debug build served by Metro on port 8081–8089)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--seconds` | yes | How long to watch (1–60) |
| `--grep` | yes | Only requests whose URL contains this |
| `--bodies` | no | Also each request's headers and text bodies (at most 4 KiB each); secrets in them are redacted |
| `--app` | yes | The app's bundle id or package, when several are connected to Metro |

##### `oximux sim rn profile`

Where the app's JavaScript spends its time: a CPU profile for a few seconds, its functions by self time

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--seconds` | yes | How long to profile (1–60) |
| `--top` | yes | How many functions to list (1–100) |
| `--app` | yes | The app's bundle id or package, when several are connected to Metro |

### `oximux mcp`

Serve the attached simulator to an outside MCP client over stdio (`{"command": "oximux", "args": ["mcp", "--worktree", "/path/to/repo"]}`). Six tools: status, observe, act, app, screenshot, wait-consent. The client asks the user for its own permission, apart from agents'

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--worktree` | yes | The worktree whose device to serve. Required unless the current directory is a worktree OxiMux knows |

### `oximux serve`

Run this machine as a headless OxiMux host.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--data-dir` | yes | The data directory (default: this machine's OxiMux data dir, shared with the desktop app so sessions and pairings are one set) |
| `--project` | yes | A project root to offer as a new-session target (repeatable; also read from <data-dir>/projects.toml) |

### `oximux pair-new`

Mint a one-time, short-lived pairing ticket on the running host.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--read-only` | no | Mint a read-only enrollment (it can watch, never act) |
| `--force-non-tty` | no | Print the ticket even though stdout is not a terminal. You are taking responsibility for where it lands |

### `oximux pair-ls`

List the host's paired devices, tier and revocation included

_No arguments._

### `oximux pair-rm`

Erase one device's enrollment (it may pair again with a fresh ticket)

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<PUBKEY>` | yes | The device's public key, as `pair-ls` printed it (64 hex chars) |

### `oximux version`

Print this CLI's build and protocol versions (offline)

_No arguments._

### `oximux update`

Replace this installation with the latest signed release

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--check` | no | Report what a release offers and exit without changing anything |

### `oximux skills`

The agent-facing guides that teach an agent to drive OxiMux

_No arguments._

#### `oximux skills ls`

List the guides this binary carries, with a one-line summary each

_No arguments._

#### `oximux skills get`

Print one guide on stdout.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<TOPIC>` | yes | The topic (see `skills ls`) |
| `--full` | no | Include the YAML frontmatter, as installed |

#### `oximux skills install`

Install the guides into the agents on this machine.

| Argument | Takes a value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--agent` | yes | One agent slug (see `agent hooks status`). Default: every agent here that already keeps skills |

Print the full command schema as JSON, for agents driving this CLI (offline — never touches the host)

_No arguments._

### `oximux completions`

Print a shell completion script on stdout (offline).
